attachments.document_title: Landlord's rent increase notice (with any covering letter)
attachments.label: A1
must_show: date from which the increase applies
whether the form approved by the canton is used (for a graduated-rent step, whether it is in writing: art. 269d para. 5)
any threat of termination in it or in the covering letter
for an index-linked increase: the old and new index values
if the landlord gave no notice at all, that absence is itself the finding (art. 269d para. 2 let. a)
attachments.text:
Rebhalde Cooperative
Wohlen

NOTIFICATION OF RENT INCREASE
Official form approved by the Canton of Aargau

Tenant: Emma Brunner
Property: 4.5-room flat, Rosenweg 54, Wohlen

Previous rent: CHF 3270 per month
New rent: CHF 3350 per month
Effective from: 1 October 2026

Reason: Adjustment of the rent in accordance with the provisions of the lease agreement of 24 December 2022.

If you consider the increase to be abusive, you may contest it with the conciliation authority within 30 days of receipt.

Wohlen, 29 June 2026
Rebhalde Cooperative
Felix Frei

questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Does the increase notice give, as its reason, higher costs for the landlord (for example higher mortgage interest or operating costs) or additional services or works by the landlord (for example a renovation)?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase is a step fixed in advance in the lease, by which the rent rises periodically by fixed amounts (graduated rent)?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Does the claim state that the landlord has announced, demanded or charged a higher rent for the dwelling, by a notice, a letter, an invoice or otherwise (whether or not on an official form)?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Does the claim state that the increase applies a clause of the lease linking the rent to an index (such as the Swiss consumer price index)?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Does the claim state that, together with the rent increase, the landlord gave notice of termination?

text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

I've attached the rent notice I received from the Rebhalde Cooperative at the end of June.

My lease, which I signed in December 2022, is a bit of a muddle. On one page there is a table saying the rent goes up by fixed amounts on certain dates. Whether this particular increase is one of those steps, I honestly can't work out. My friend Nina Fankhauser, who read the contract with me, is fairly sure it is, because the date matches the table. When I asked Mr Felix Frei, he said the table was "no longer relevant" but wouldn't explain why. So that part is still a mystery.

What I do know is that the lease also contains a clause tying the rent to the Swiss consumer price index, and as far as I understand, this increase applies that index clause.

The notice, dated 29 June 2026, tells me my rent for the flat at Rosenweg 54 in Wohlen will go from CHF 3270 to CHF 3350 a month from 1 October 2026. For our household that is a noticeable jump on top of everything else getting more expensive.

Could you help me understand whether this is correct, and whether it matters if it's an index increase or one of the steps from the table? I'd like to know if I should contest it before any deadline runs out.

Thank you,
Emma Brunner
